findings.text: blocking: _LIVE_ROW_FIELDS (reckon/mcp.py:262-327) is a hand-copied duplicate of the vocabulary reckon.crew.query._live_field_vocabulary derives, and it omits COMMON_RUN_FIELDS (reckon/crew/query.py:205) which the derived set folds in at reckon/crew/query.py:174. A live read naming that field is now refused before storage while the view still serves it: at head mcp._crew(project='fixture', view='live', fields=['section']) answers {'ok': False, 'error': 'crew_error', 'detail': "unknown live fields 'section'; live fields are backend, budget_overrun, ..., worktree"}, whereas the view's own predicate accepts it — PYTHONPATH=<head tree> python -I -c "from reckon.crew.query import _refuse_unknown_live_fields; _refuse_unknown_live_fields(['section'], [], with_mine=False)" returns without raising. reckon/crew/query.py:199-205 declares section the field that vocabulary exists to guarantee ('a run is dispatched for one section of one plan, and every view that lists runs names it'), and the live view routes its rows through project_run_rows (reckon/crew/query.py:363), which fills section from the run's pointer. Repair is one import: COMMON_RUN_FIELDS is exported beside LIVE_OVERRUN_FIELDS and LIVE_PLACEMENT_FIELDS, which this node did import. Until it is added, the pre-flight trades the defect it repairs for a false refusal of a served field.

non-blocking: _requested_field_names is a verbatim copy of the function the repository already owns at reckon/crew/query.py:104 — the same four branches, body for body, with one word of the docstring changed — so the parsing of one request's fields now has two owners that can drift apart exactly as _LIVE_ROW_FIELDS did. The owner module is already imported by this diff for RUN_SCOPES, RUN_SOURCES, LIVE_OVERRUN_FIELDS and LIVE_PLACEMENT_FIELDS.

non-blocking: the view pre-flight compares the raw argument against VIEW_NAMES, where the view's own validator strips and lowercases first (reckon/mcp_views.py:2087-2101: selected = (view or 'summary').strip().lower()). mcp._read_plan_tool(project='fixture', view='RAW') now answers {"ok": false, "error": "invalid_view", "detail": "unknown view 'RAW'; view must be one of detail, history, raw, schema, section, summary or version"} while normalize_view('RAW') returns 'raw', so a request the tool answered before this change is refused now; the same shape sits at reckon/mcp.py:2182 for the roadmap views.

non-blocking: the field pre-flight covers only view == 'live'. The runs view carries its own field vocabulary (reckon/crew/query.py:115 _refuse_unknown_fields, reached through _selected_fields at reckon/crew/query.py:148), and a malformed crew view=runs fields=[...] request still reads the pointers and the ledger before that refusal, so the plan's 'Field names ... are checked against their declared vocabularies first' is delivered for one of the two views that take fields.

non-blocking: assert "dispatched_at" in detail is satisfied by any refusal whose text echoes the name it was handed, so the two sides of the assertion move together with the value the test supplied and it would stay green for a checker that refused every field name. Nothing in the file asserts the opposite direction — that a valid live field list is not refused — which is why the blocking defect above passes this gate: the gate proves a malformed request is refused, never that a well-formed one still is served.

non-blocking: the module docstring carries incident and changelog prose rather than mechanism — 'on 2026-10-23 a crew view live call naming an unknown field waited over 120 s before it was refused' (line 7) and 'On the script's revision before the argument checks moved ahead of the first read, the crew live field call reached the stub and the test failed here' (lines 11-12) — which the repository's comment rule forbids in source. The mechanism sentence around it ('Refusing it after the first file read makes the answer wait on whatever storage is doing') carries the same information without the dated incident or the previous revision's behaviour.

FINDING reckon/mcp.py:262 blocking: _LIVE_ROW_FIELDS is a hand-copied duplicate of the vocabulary reckon.crew.query._live_field_vocabulary derives and it omits COMMON_RUN_FIELDS, so the pre-flight refuses a field the live view serves — mcp._crew(project='fixture', view='live', fields=['section']) answers unknown live fields for section while _refuse_unknown_live_fields(['section'], [], with_mine=False) accepts it; one import repairs it.
FINDING reckon/mcp.py:336 non-blocking: _requested_field_names is a verbatim copy of the function the repository already owns at reckon/crew/query.py:104, so the parsing of one request's fields has two owners that can drift.

FINDING reckon/mcp.py:370 non-blocking: the field pre-flight covers only the live view, so a malformed crew view=runs fields request still reads the pointers before its refusal at reckon/crew/query.py:115.
FINDING tests/test_a_malformed_request_is_refused_before_storage.py:61 non-blocking: the assertion is satisfied by a refusal that echoes the name it was handed, and no case asserts a valid live field list is still served, which is why the false refusal at reckon/mcp.py:262 passes this gate.
